newsitem.title: USA: Centennial seeking settlement in lawsuits.
newsitem.headline: Centennial seeking settlement in lawsuits.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc is seeking an early settlement to the more than 30 class action lawsuits against the company filed by more than 1,000 shareholders, lawyers said Thursday.
"We'd like to get a settlement dialogue going," Jeff Rudman, a lawyer for Centennial, told reporters following a brief court hearing.

Glen DeValerio, representing a slew of plaintiffs' lawyers filling the room, told the court that more than 1,000 shareholders have so far signed onto the more than 30 class action lawsuits filed against the software company.
More shareholders may seek to join the suits, DeValerio added.

Centennial founder Emanuel Pinez, who was arrested in February on charges of insider trading violations, allegedly manipulated the company's inventories to inflate sales, according to U.S. prosecutors.
Centennial said in late February that it will have to restate its earnings for the years 1994 to 1996 and the first half of 1997 to report losses instead of profits.
Pinez, who was denied bail and sits in jail, has pled not guilty to the charges.
The Billerica, Mass.-based company, which was the best-performing Big Board stock last year, was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange in early March.
